QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_13

question.text: Ms. Kavita Menon, manager of Sahyadri Opportunities AIF, sees tenure expiring on 30-Jun-2026. Under the 2023 SEBI amendments, the 'Liquidation Period' available for selling remaining assets before triggering in-specie distribution is:

answer.text: Until LPs vote otherwise, with no hard cap

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the 2023 SEBI (AIF) amendment, the Liquidation Period is one year following expiry of the scheme's tenure (or extended tenure) within which the AIF must fully liquidate its assets. The Trap: 6 months understates the prescribed window. 2 years confuses the Liquidation Period with the tenure-extension cap. 'No hard cap' is wrong — a definite one-year window is prescribed. Note: If assets remain unsold at the end of the Liquidation Period, the AIF may use the in-specie distribution route or enter a Dissolution Period, both of which are governed by separate SEBI conditions.
